# Workflows

Start one with `/factory <request>` (the orchestrator picks the workflow and size and says why) or name it: `/factory fix …`, `/factory data …`. Each workflow is a JSON file in `plugins/factory/workflows/`, validated by the engine and snapshotted into the job when it starts, so an upgrade never changes a running job.

Limits (defaults, per job; `.factory/config.json` changes them): 40 agent runs, 3 review rounds, 2 attempts per step, 4 agents at once. Hitting one stops the job for a human; it never continues silently.

| Workflow | Use when | Ends with |
|---|---|---|
| [`feature`](#feature) | Adding or changing product behaviour, APIs or full-stack features. | a local merge (or a ready branch) |
| [`fix`](#fix) | A defect, failing test, production incident or regression. | a local merge (or a ready branch) |
| [`quick`](#quick) | Small, unambiguous changes: a query, a config tweak, a focused refactor, a doc fix. | a local merge (or a ready branch) |
| [`research`](#research) | Choosing a library or approach, understanding a system or standard, feasibility questions. | a delivered report |
| [`review`](#review) | Assessing a codebase, preparing a refactor, due diligence, tech-debt triage. | a delivered report |
| [`data`](#data) | Queries, pipelines, data models, schema changes, data-quality checks, analytical performance. | a local merge (or a ready branch) |
| [`infra`](#infra) | Terraform/IaC, Kubernetes, CI/CD, networking, IAM, observability changes. | a local merge (or a ready branch) |
| [`refactor`](#refactor) | Legacy modernisation, tech-debt reduction, restructuring without behaviour change. | a local merge (or a ready branch) |
| [`perf`](#perf) | Slow endpoints, queries, jobs or pages; capacity work. | a local merge (or a ready branch) |
| [`security`](#security) | Security assessments, dependency audits, pre-release security checks. | a delivered report |
| [`docs`](#docs) | READMEs, architecture docs, API references, runbooks, ADRs, release notes. | a local merge (or a ready branch) |

## feature

**Feature.** Specify, (plan,) build, review and merge a change to the codebase.

Use when: Adding or changing product behaviour, APIs or full-stack features.

1. Set up worktree — worktree + branch `factory/<job>`, dependencies installed
2. Specify — `product-analyst` writes `spec.md`
3. Plan — `architect` writes `design.md` *(only when size is M or L)*
4. Plan approval — human gate (`/factory build <job>` to continue, `/factory rework <job> <note>`) *(only when size is L or policy `require_plan_approval`)*
5. Build — `builder` builds (plan tasks first when a plan exists), commits, writes `build.md`
6. Review — review panel: always code, security; +ux, ui when ui; +performance when perf; any CHANGES loops back to `build`
7. Approve — `approver` decides APPROVE or ESCALATE
8. Merge — local merge into the base branch (or a ready branch with `deliver: branch`); never pushed

## quick

**Quick task.** One specialist does a small, well-defined change; a code review and the approver gate it.

Use when: Small, unambiguous changes: a query, a config tweak, a focused refactor, a doc fix.

1. Set up worktree — worktree + branch `factory/<job>`, dependencies installed
2. Build — `$param.agent` builds (plan tasks first when a plan exists), commits, writes `build.md`
3. Review — review panel: always code; +ux, ui when ui; any CHANGES loops back to `build`
4. Approve — `approver` decides APPROVE or ESCALATE
5. Merge — local merge into the base branch (or a ready branch with `deliver: branch`); never pushed

## research

**Research.** Investigate a technical question with sources and a recommendation; no code changes.

Use when: Choosing a library or approach, understanding a system or standard, feasibility questions.

1. Set up worktree — worktree + branch `factory/<job>`
2. Investigate — in parallel: `researcher` → `research.md`, `codebase-analyst` → `context.md`
3. Deliver — delivers `the report`; nothing is merged

## review

**Codebase review.** Audit an existing codebase for correctness, security, performance and test gaps, then synthesise a prioritised improvement plan.

Use when: Assessing a codebase, preparing a refactor, due diligence, tech-debt triage.

1. Set up worktree — worktree + branch `factory/<job>`, dependencies installed
2. Map codebase — `codebase-analyst` writes `context.md`
3. Audit — in parallel: `code-reviewer` → `audit-code.md`, `security-engineer` → `audit-security.md`, `performance-engineer` → `audit-performance.md`, `test-architect` → `audit-tests.md`
4. Synthesise — `architect` writes `report.md`
5. Deliver — delivers `the report`; nothing is merged

## Review panel

Code and security reviewers sit on every panel. UX and UI reviewers join when UI files change (globs: `*.vue`, `*.svelte`, `*.tsx`, `*.jsx`, `*.css`, `*.scss`, …) or the builder declares `UI impact: yes`; the performance engineer joins for perf and data work or hot paths. Membership only grows across rounds, every seat records why it was picked, and a round waits for every reviewer before the builder is resumed.
